findings.title: Module-level `assert` guards bucket completeness
findings.description: `_BUCKET_ROWS` is checked against `TickSessionStatus` with a bare `assert`. Python strips asserts under `-O`, so the guard silently disappears there. If a new status is added, `p.buckets[...]` lookups would still work because `buckets` is built from the full enum. The new status would just be missing from the rendered output. This is low risk. An explicit `raise RuntimeError` or a unit test would make the guard unconditional.

findings.title: `raw_counts` scans `tick_trade` with no load-tier test
findings.description: This is the only full-range `tick_trade` scan. It is bounded by the first open and last close, but the tests only seed a handful of rows. The Python rules ask for a load test on paths that could exhaust resources, and a wide `--start/--end` range on a hypertable is such a path. `coverage` is a manual CLI verb, so this is not blocking. It is still worth adding a bounded-latency check or documenting the expected range limits.

findings.title: Inclusive boundary on session intervals
findings.description: The join uses `t.ts_event BETWEEN s.open_ns AND s.close_ns`, which is inclusive on both ends. A row at an instant shared by one session's close and the next session's open would be counted twice. CME sessions normally have a gap between them, so this is unlikely. If the calendar ever yields abutting sessions, `close_ns` should be exclusive. I did not check how the ledger side defines its session boundaries.

findings.title: Minor quality items in the status builder
findings.description:
- `[c for c in lines if c not in spreads]` compares dataclasses by value, so it is O(n·m). Filtering on `instrument_class != SPREAD_CLASS` is simpler.
- `_read` and `build_coverage`'s `read` helper type `conn` as `Any`, which loses strict-pyright coverage at that seam. `Conn` is available and would be more precise.
- The refactor that extracts `utc_midnight` and `days_touched`, and removes the duplicate `_midnight`, is a good DRY change. Behavior is preserved, including the `[start, end)` filter in `session_days`.

findings.title: Exception handling, exit-code mapping and DB safety
findings.description:
- `TickDatabaseUnreachable` subclasses `TickPreflightError`, so the writers keep their existing preflight mapping. `status` and `coverage` map it to the storage exit through the new `storage` parameter.
- `run_mapped` is a documented process-boundary handler that re-raises unmapped exceptions.
- `connect_migrated` closes the connection on failure, and `_read` closes it in `finally`.
- All SQL is parameterized. The f-string fragments are module constants, not user input.
- The tests delete rows only in the throwaway `migrated_tick_db` fixture, and none read the production URL variable.
